[THOUGHT]  
The clinical presentation is highly characteristic of an idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, specifically immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM). Key diagnostic anchors include: (1) subacute, progressive *proximal* muscle weakness — consistent with myopathic distribution; (2) absence of extramuscular features (no rash, dysphagia, interstitial lung disease, or cardiac symptoms), which makes dermatomyositis and antisynthetase syndrome less likely; (3) markedly elevated CK and aldolase — reflecting ongoing myofiber necrosis; (4) EMG showing myopathic changes with irritability, supporting inflammatory myopathy over metabolic or dystrophic causes; and (5) muscle biopsy revealing *endomysial CD8+ T-lymphocyte infiltration* — a hallmark of IMNM (distinct from perimysial inflammation in dermatomyositis or perivascular inflammation in vasculitis). While anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR results are pending, the biopsy finding is *diagnostically definitive* for IMNM: these antibodies are supportive but not required for diagnosis, as seronegative IMNM is well-recognized and histologically distinct. MRI STIR and malignancy screening are appropriate next steps but do not alter the core diagnosis. The absence of thyroid or cardiac biomarker assessment is irrelevant to establishing IMNM — those tests serve only to exclude mimics (e.g., hypothyroid myopathy, myocarditis), which are already unlikely given the biopsy-proven immune-mediated necrosis.

[EVIDENCE]  
- Subacute, progressive proximal muscle weakness (stairs, overhead activities) over several months  
- No systemic, cutaneous, bulbar, or respiratory involvement  
- Elevated creatine kinase and aldolase  
- Electromyography shows abnormalities consistent with inflammatory myopathy  
- Muscle biopsy demonstrates endomysial CD8+ T-lymphocyte infiltration  
- Serologic testing for anti-SRP/anti-HMGCR ordered but pending (i.e., not yet available to confirm or refute)

[GAPS]  
- Anti-SRP and anti-HMGCR antibody results are pending — would help subclassify IMNM and inform prognosis/treatment responsiveness  
- Thigh MRI STIR findings not yet reported — would quantify active edema/inflammation but not change diagnosis  
- Malignancy screening status unknown — relevant for risk stratification but not diagnostic  
- Thyroid function and cardiac biomarkers unassessed — appropriate for ruling out mimics but not needed to establish IMNM given definitive biopsy  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM)
